newsitem.title: GERMANY: FOCUS - Linde orders flat, but outlook better.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Linde orders flat, but outlook better.

text.p: Europe's top fork-lift truck maker Linde AG on Wednesday reported business was flat in the first nine months of 1996 due to a domestic market slump but stuck to its forecast for higher full-year earnings.

The German engineering group said incoming orders in the first nine months rose just 1.8 percent to 6.44 billion marks ($4.22 billion), reflecting sluggish demand in Germany for goods handling equipment, its biggest division, and industrial gases.

However, sales rose 6.8 percent to 6.4 billion marks, a figure Linde described as satisfactory. It noted sales would have risen 7.5 percent excluding its plant automation division where business tended to be sporadic.

"We expect a sales rise of around five percent to 8.7 billion marks for Linde this year and a further improvement in earnings. Declines at home will be offset by higher returns abroad," the group said in a statement, repeating forecasts made at the half-year stage.
The stock market took the news as neutral and Linde's stock was unchanged by mid-session at 955 marks.
In the first three quarters, Linde's domestic sales slipped slightly to 2.31 billion marks from 2.38 billion, with plant automation sales falling to 106 million marks from 152 million.

Foreign sales, however, rose to 4.1 billion marks from 3.6 billion. Gains were registered by all business divisions, especially goods handling equipment, where turnover rose to 1.9 billion marks from 1.6 billion.
Group staff increased by 370 to 30,483, largely due to first-time consolidation of new units.

Linde noted there had been an overall economic improvement in the U.S and also in Japan this year, following a long period of stagnation. Growth was moderate in most other industrialised countries, but generally better than in Germany.
